findings.failure_path: the skip triggers on any prompt that merely starts with <task-notification>, so a user pasting a background-completion envelope to ask about it loses that turn's task entry although the acceptance keeps the entry for any prompt other than the host's envelope turn
findings.smallest_fix: tighten the check to the full envelope shape, e.g. lstripped prefix <task-notification> and rstripped suffix </task-notification>, before skipping

concern_results.conclusion: Bands sum input+cache-read+cache-write of the newest non-sidechain assistant usage with positive total in the bounded tail, fire at-or-above 300k/600k once per band, join a block result without touching its reason, and stay quiet for below-band, Codex, synthetic zero-usage and usage-less tails; the envelope turn gets {} while unparseable/oversized input keeps the entry; the receipt counts review/challenge only, keeps first_recorded_at, restarts on bad prior receipts, and the checkpoint starts at the sixth run — consistent with acceptance except the prefix-only envelope test reported below.

The notice exposes only a count; the prompt is read bounded (1 MiB) and never echoed; the prior receipt is opened O_NOFOLLOW relative to the no-follow receipt dir, fstat-checked, capped at 64 KiB; temp-plus-rename replaces a planted symlink without following it; no secret, permission, egress or filesystem-mutation surface added.

Every new read fails soft: a notice error drops only the notice, closed/unreadable stdin and bad JSON keep the task entry, and a missing, corrupt, oversized or linked prior receipt restarts the count while the new receipt is still written; concurrent gate runs can only undercount by one, delaying an advisory object.

Each behavior has a test that fails on main (three Stop cases, two task-entry cases including closed stdin, three gate checks covering threshold, legacy, corrupt, oversized and linked receipts), plus a nine-mutation kill walk with a green control and pre-registered blind replays; evidence is appropriate, though no adversarial-challenge pass over the hooks is shown (reported).

Only additive receipt/output fields; the hook still emits exactly one JSON object with exit 0; legacy receipts read as one prior run; no flag, gate, switch, permission or compatibility layer added, and scope stays inside the requester's efficiency/cost/token ask.
Plugin update ships it and a single-commit revert restores prior behavior; rolled-back code ignores the new receipt fields; no migration or irreversible step.

The count and first timestamp are visible in the receipt and gate output and the notice states the measured size; the task-entry skip is silent by design and is documented in the script comment and the round plan.

Cost shares, the 34% injection figure and the 13–49 loop counts are stated as one-month, one-product-line measurements; the same-class sentence is measured at ceiling and explicitly not claimed as a behavior change; the withdrawn counting reference claims nothing.

The shared gate gains one bounded no-follow read and two receipt fields; the checkpoint never blocks or authorizes and deleting the receipt only restarts an advisory count; packet, verdict, egress and reviewer-selection logic are untouched.

Root and scripts contracts are honored (synthetic test data, no business names or private paths, RED-baseline tests before behavior, no dead cited paths in the diff, no contract file loosened); hooks/AGENTS.md requires adversarial challenge before landing for non-wording hook changes and the packet carries no such evidence and no declared deviation — reported below.
